title: My Slow Morning Routine (The Realistic Version)
creator: Dee Okonkwo
description:
No 5am ice baths here. Just daylight, a screaming cat, overnight oats and a journal.

This video is sponsored by MUD\WTR. Get 15% off your first order plus a free frother at https://mudwtr.com/dee

Overnight oats recipe in the pinned comment.

sentences.t: Good morning, it's six forty-five, and I'm going to be honest with you, I hit snooze twice.
This is my realistic morning routine, not the five a.m. ice bath version, the version where I'm a person with a job and a cat who screams.
First thing, I open the blinds, and I try to get some daylight in my eyes before I look at my phone.
I don't always manage that, but on the days I do, I genuinely feel more awake by eight.
Next, I feed Biscuit, because she will not let me do anything else until she's eaten.
She's been sitting by the bowl since six, judging me.
Then I put the kettle on, and while it boils I do about five minutes of stretching on the kitchen floor.
Nothing fancy, just a few cat-cows, a hamstring stretch, and some neck rolls, because I sleep like a pretzel.
Breakfast is usually overnight oats that I made the night before, with frozen berries, a spoon of peanut butter, and a little bit of honey.
Making them the night before is the single best thing I've done for my mornings, because the version of me at seven a.m. is not going to cook.
Okay, the kettle's done, and this next part is something I've been wanting to tell you about, because today's video is sponsored by Mud Water.
Mud Water is a coffee alternative made from cacao, mushrooms like lion's mane and chaga, and spices like cinnamon and turmeric.
It has about a seventh of the caffeine of a cup of coffee, so I get a gentle lift without the jitters and without the two p.m. crash.
I used to be a three-coffee-a-day person, and switching my first cup to this has made my mornings so much calmer.
I make it with hot water and a splash of oat milk, give it a quick froth, and it tastes kind of like a spiced hot chocolate, but earthier.
If you want to try it, go to Mud Water dot com slash dee and you'll get fifteen percent off your first order, plus a free frother.
Then I sit by the window for ten minutes with my drink and my journal.
I write down three things, what I'm worried about, what I'm looking forward to, and one thing I want to get done no matter what.
Some days the worry list is long, and that's fine, it's better on paper than in my head.
Then I shower, get dressed, and do the bare minimum of makeup, which is honestly just sunscreen and mascara.
At about seven forty, I check my phone for the first time, and I try to answer messages before opening anything with a feed.
That's the part I fail at most, I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
Then I pack my lunch, give Biscuit one last head scratch, and leave by eight fifteen.
So that's it, my realistic morning.
It's not perfect, it's not aesthetic, and I definitely didn't wake up at five.
But it's the first routine I've actually stuck to for more than a month, and I think that's because it's built around things I like.
Let me know what your mornings look like down in the comments, especially if you've got a screaming cat too.
See you in the next one.
